penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: ETL/ODBC pipeline setup and migration almost always requires per-customer technical configuration, schema mapping, and onboarding that cannot be fully automated by Claude + a prompt.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Enterprise IT buyers at subsidiaries expect scoping calls, demos, and implementation support before purchasing data integration tooling.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Ongoing support for database connectivity, driver compatibility, and schema drift requires human technical judgment.

rationale: The buyer is a real corporate IT person with genuine pain and clear willingness to pay for ETL tooling — that part is solid. However, building a credible ODBC ETL product requires custom infrastructure, driver compatibility layers, and deep integration work that is far beyond what Claude + prompts + a Stripe link can deliver in a week or a month. Operational autonomy is critically low: every customer deployment requires hands-on technical configuration, making this a consulting engagement, not an automated micro-service.
solution_plan: This cannot realistically be built and run as an autonomous micro-service by a solo non-technical operator. A functioning ODBC ETL product requires database driver engineering, schema introspection, incremental replication logic, and per-customer setup — none of which Claude can automate end-to-end. Attempting to sell this without that infrastructure would result in either overpromising to enterprise buyers or delivering a glorified consulting arrangement that consumes Youval's time on every deal. Drop this opportunity.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai (score 3, floor 6), operational_autonomy (score 3, floor 7). Even without penalties the weighted total is modest; with penalties it is effectively disqualified.
